**Helping Every Child Succeed: Our New Approach to Math Classes**

Dear Parents and Carers,

We know that you want the absolute best for your child. You want them to finish school with the skills, confidence, and qualifications they need for a bright future. 

We are writing to share an important change we are making to our math classes this year, and to explain why we are making it. 

### What is changing?
In the past, we used a system called **"streaming"** or **"setting."** This meant we tested children and split them into different math classes based on their test scores—usually a "top" group, a "middle" group, and a "bottom" group.

This year, we are moving to **mixed-attainment teaching**. This means students of all different math levels will learn together in the same classroom. 

We know this is a big change, and we know many of you might feel worried about it. You might be asking: *Will my child be held back? Will my child get left behind?* 

We want to reassure you that we have made this decision because **research and experience show it is the best way to help every single student do better in math.**

Here is why we are making this change:

---

### 1. We want to unlock every child’s potential
When children are put into a "bottom" or "middle" group early on, they often start to believe, *"I’m just not good at math."* Once a child gets put into a lower group, it is very hard for them to move up. They are often given easier work, which means they never get the chance to try the harder math that they need for their final exams.

By keeping students together, we keep the door open for everyone. We believe **every child can do well in math** if they are given the right support and high expectations.

### 2. It helps students who find math difficult
When students who struggle with math are grouped only with other students who struggle, they don't get to hear how other people solve problems. 

In our new classrooms, students will work together. Hearing a classmate explain how they solved a problem in a different way is one of the best ways to learn. Your child will not be left to struggle alone; they will have the support of their teacher and their classmates.

### 3. It helps students who are already good at math
If your child is already very good at math, you might worry they will be bored. We promise you, they won't be. 

In mixed classes, we don't just give quick students "more of the same" easy worksheets. Instead, we give them **deeper, more challenging puzzles** that make them think hard. 

Also, one of the best ways to truly master math is to explain it to someone else. When stronger students help their classmates, it actually strengthens their own understanding and prepares them for top marks in exams.

### 4. It teaches real-world skills
In the workplace, no one is sorted into "top" and "bottom" groups. Whether you work in construction, healthcare, retail, or technology, you have to work with all kinds of people. Learning together teaches our students how to communicate, help others, and solve problems as a team.

---

### What will a math lesson look like now?
Our teachers have been training hard for this change. In a typical lesson:
* **Everyone starts together:** The teacher will introduce a topic or a puzzle that everyone can understand.
* **Different paths:** The teacher will give different levels of challenge. Students who need extra help will get it, while students who understand quickly will be pushed to try harder, deeper questions.
* **No one is labeled:** No child will feel the shame of being in the "slow" class, and no child will feel the pressure of having to be perfect in the "top" class.

### We are in this together
We know that many of us had difficult experiences with math when we were at school. You do not need to be a math expert to support your child. The most important thing you can do is tell them that **with hard work, they can learn anything.**

We are fully committed to making sure this change helps your child succeed. If you have any questions, or if you would like to come in and talk to us about how we are supporting your child, our doors are always open.

Thank you for your support and partnership.

Warm regards,

**[School Principal/Head of Mathematics]**  
**[School Name]**
